investment_signals.headline: Spotify reported Q2 2026 growth and a record gross margin.
investment_signals.detail: The Q2 2026 update reported 777M total MAUs, 300M Premium subscribers and 494M ad-supported MAUs at June 30. Total revenue was €4,777M, gross margin 33.4%, operating income €655M and free cash flow €797M; Premium revenue was €4,331M and Premium ARPU was €4.89, up 7% year over year.
investment_signals.metric_name: Premium subscribers / MAUs / ARPU / gross margin / FCF

investment_signals.headline: Spotify guided to Q3 2026 growth with €670M operating income.
investment_signals.detail: Q3 guidance was 788M MAUs, 305M Premium subscribers, €5.0B total revenue, 32.9% gross margin and €670M operating income. The guidance was stated as subject to substantial uncertainty.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify said Q2 Premium ARPU growth reflected price-increase benefits.
investment_signals.detail: Premium ARPU was €4.89, up 7% year over year and 7.4% on a constant-currency basis. Spotify said that excluding FX, ARPU growth was driven by price-increase benefits, partly offset by product and market mix.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify announced a $1 US Premium Individual increase.
investment_signals.detail: Spotify said it was updating Premium pricing in the US, Estonia and Latvia. Reuters reported the US Individual price would rise from $11.99 to $12.99 per month, with the change applying from subscribers’ February billing dates; the current official US page shows $12.99 recurring.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify announced a multi-region Premium price increase.
investment_signals.detail: Spotify’s newsroom said subscribers in South Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific would receive emails about the update. Reuters reported the Individual price would rise to €11.99 per month from €10.99 in selected markets, with the change beginning in September 2025; the official notice did not enumerate every country or exact effective date.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify reported Q1 2026 revenue and profitability growth.
investment_signals.detail: Q1 2026 total revenue was €4,533M, gross margin 33.0%, operating income €715M and free cash flow €824M. Premium subscribers reached 293M and MAUs 761M; Premium ARPU was €4.76 and Spotify said constant-currency ARPU was up 5.7% year over year, driven by price increases partly offset by mix.
investment_signals.metric_name: Premium subscribers / MAUs / gross margin / operating income / FCF

investment_signals.headline: Spotify expanded music-video access to Premium users in the US and Canada.
investment_signals.detail: Reuters reported that Spotify made music videos available to Premium subscribers in the US and Canada, positioning the move against YouTube. Reuters said users who discovered a track with a video were 34% more likely to stream it again and 24% more likely to save or share it the following week.

competitor_reactions.action: expanded music-video access in Spotify’s US and Canada competitive set
competitor_reactions.detail: Reuters described Spotify’s music-video expansion as a challenge to YouTube; no verified YouTube price response to the Spotify increases was found in the retrieved sources.

consumer_reaction.price_sentiment_summary: The US App Store listing showed 4.8 out of 5 from 42M ratings. No country-specific quantified price-sentiment share was visible in the retrieved listing.

The US Google Play listing showed 4.3 stars and 36.4M reviews in the prominent header; a lower display showed 34.2M, so the page is internally inconsistent. No country-specific quantified price-sentiment share was visible.

Variety reported US prices rising from $11.99 to $12.99 for Individual, $16.99 to $18.99 for Duo, $19.99 to $21.99 for Family and $5.99 to $6.99 for Student. The article characterized price hikes as usually greeted with “annoyance if not outrage,” without providing a quantified survey share.

A Trustpilot review said the service was “a bit pricey”; the page showed 5,850 reviews but the cited review had no visible country or publication date. Trustpilot stated its company rating was unavailable due to a breach of guidelines.

key_findings: Spotify’s Q2 2026 Premium subscriber base reached 300M (+9% YoY) and Premium ARPU reached €4.89 (+7% YoY); Spotify explicitly attributed constant-currency ARPU growth to price-increase benefits partly offset by mix (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Q2 2026 gross margin was 33.4%, operating income €655M and free cash flow €797M, while trailing-12-month free cash flow was €3.3B (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Spotify’s latest verified US price is $12.99/month after a January 2026 announcement of a move from $11.99; the page’s trial is $0 for one month for eligible new users (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-01-15/premium-pricing-update/; https://www.spotify.com/us/premium/).

The August 2025 international move was reported as €10.99 to €11.99 in selected markets across six regions, but Spotify did not publish a complete country/effective-date table in the retrieved notice (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-08-04/upcoming-changes-to-spotify-premium-subscriptions/).

Spotify’s current page set shows materially differentiated local pricing and plan architecture, including Standard, Basic, Platinum and audiobook-inclusive offerings in some markets (for example Korea, UAE, South Africa and Indonesia), so mix—not only headline price—is a relevant ARPU variable (https://www.spotify.com/kr-ko/premium/; https://www.spotify.com/ae-en/premium/).

US consumer measures were 4.8/5 from 42M App Store ratings and 4.3 stars from 36.4M Google Play reviews as displayed by the retrieved listings; Google Play showed an inconsistent lower review count and no quantified price-sentiment share (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/spotify-music-and-podcasts/id324684580; https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music&hl=en_US).

No derived US Spotify-versus-Apple/YouTube comparison is emitted in this run because the fetched official Apple Music US page did not expose a recurring Individual price in page content; a same-currency comparison is therefore a documented gap rather than an inference.
analyst_summary.hike_pattern: The sourced history shows two observable waves inside the 24-month window: the selected-market announcement on 2025-08-04, reported as €10.99 to €11.99 (+9.1%) with September 2025 timing but no exact effective date, followed by the US/Estonia/Latvia announcement on 2026-01-15, with the US Individual moving $11.99 to $12.99 (+8.3%) and billing-date implementation reported from February. The retrieved evidence is not sufficient to claim which country always moves first or a complete cadence.
bull_points: Price increases are translating into reported ARPU growth: Q2 Premium ARPU was €4.89, up 7% YoY, with Spotify attributing constant-currency growth to price-increase benefits (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Q2 2026 delivered 300M Premium subscribers, 33.4% gross margin and €797M FCF, all directly relevant to Subscribers × ARPU → margin → cash conversion (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).
Spotify guided to 305M Premium subscribers and €670M operating income for Q3 2026 (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).
bear_points: The August 2025 price announcement was broad but not country-specific, preventing a fully auditable country-by-country hike cadence (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-08-04/upcoming-changes-to-spotify-premium-subscriptions/).

Spotify’s Q2 guidance included 32.9% gross margin versus 33.4% in Q2 actuals, so the guided sequential margin level was lower (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).
The fetched live-page evidence does not provide churn or retention figures, and trial/promotional prices can differ from recurring list prices (https://www.spotify.com/us/premium/).
watch_items_next_5_days: Recheck Spotify newsroom and local /premium pages for any price or tier changes, especially US, Canada, Europe and high-growth India/Indonesia (https://newsroom.spotify.com/; https://www.spotify.com/us/premium/).

Check Spotify IR for Q3 2026 earnings publication and update Premium subscribers, MAUs, ARPU, gross margin, operating income and FCF against Q3 guidance (https://investors.spotify.com/financials/default.aspx).

Recheck Apple Music/Apple One and YouTube Premium localized storefronts for country-specific price responses; record announcement and effective dates separately (https://www.apple.com/; https://www.youtube.com/premium).

Monitor regulatory disclosures and SEC filings for app-store fees, DMA or antitrust developments that can alter realized ARPU or margin (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001639920).
data_gaps: No official localized Spotify price was captured for Switzerland (CH); the fetched page was a 404.
Full Spotify tier coverage is incomplete across the 36 requested countries; missing Duo, Family, Student, Basic, Lite, Platinum and audiobook-inclusive tiers are not inferred.
Most requested-country Apple Music/Apple One and YouTube Premium/Music Premium prices were not captured from official localized pages, so cross-country FX comparisons are omitted.
No country-specific churn/retention metric or analyst price-target note with auditable pricing assumptions was found in the retrieved sources.
No country-specific, dated quantified consumer price-sentiment series was found; the available Variety and Trustpilot evidence is qualitative or lacks market/date detail.
The selected-market 2025 hike lacks a complete country list and exact effective dates; sourcing the affected subscriber communications or billing notices would close this gap.
Derived metrics are omitted because a directly page-extracted US Apple Music Individual recurring price was not available alongside the Spotify and YouTube prices.

run_schedule.weekly_production_schedule: Run each day at 13:15 UTC; publish a dated JSON delta plus current snapshot. On business days, reconcile official IR/SEC and newsroom first, then local pricing and storefronts.

implementation_notes: Use exact localized URL and page retrieval date; do not substitute a generic USD page for another country.
Parse recurring price separately from introductory/trial price and retain verbatim trial wording.
Detect plan cards and product-name changes (Standard, Basic, Lite, Platinum, audiobooks) before comparing prices.
For every new price, diff against the prior snapshot; require an official page or dated press/filing source before emitting a change.
Treat unknown effective dates as unknown rather than deriving them from “next month” or billing-date language.
Only compute derived comparisons when Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube Premium Individual prices plus a same-date FX rate are all present.
Capture App Store/Google Play rating and review-count strings verbatim and flag inconsistent duplicate displays rather than reconciling them.
